• Ecosystem: query libraries, docs, users, a company.
So the one-line diff: Joern is the finished platform version of your architecture, in someone else's runtime, language, and graph format — and it can't be borrowed piecemeal. Your counter isn't
"I'll rebuild Joern" (that's the heaviness you flinched from); it's the bake-off's actual question: does the engine — the one piece Joern has and you haven't finished — justify adopting a
platform, or does a native lab over your JSONL hit the same numbers at a tenth the weight? The honest caveat I keep in the plan: if Joern humiliates the field, its frontends are genuinely good,
and "parse with Joern, keep your rails" becomes the serious conversation — with the cost that your parity/oracle machinery then has to be rebuilt against a black-box CPG.
